headline: Learning-based priors and adaptive acquisition reshape cryo-EM and electron microscopy
label: Computational Imaging Reconstruction Methods
summary: Generative priors and ML-driven acquisition now target cryo-EM heterogeneity and connectomic imaging throughput directly.
synthesis: The common thread is computational inference placed between noisy measurement and structural or connectomic readout. The cryoFM preprint couples a flow-matching generative model trained on cryo-EM densities with likelihood models in Bayesian posterior sampling to denoise and refine maps. The TRPV1 benchmark evaluates five heterogeneity methods (3DFlex, 3DVA, cryoDRGN, ManifoldEM, Bayesian reweighting) on public ligand-bound TRPV1 data and introduces AnaVox for analysis. SmartEM operates at an earlier stage, applying machine learning during real-time SEM acquisition to rescan only selected regions, reported as roughly seven-fold faster connectomic imaging in nematode and mouse samples. What is new is learned priors entering the reconstruction step for cryo-EM, and learning embedded within the electron microscopy acquisition loop.
